name: Distal Myopathy with Early Respiratory Muscle Involvement

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Proposed Diagnostic Criteria for Distal Myopathy with Early Respiratory Involvement

criteria.description: Presence of progressive distal muscle weakness predominantly affecting distal limb muscles
Early onset of respiratory muscle weakness leading to restrictive ventilatory defect
Muscle biopsy showing myopathic changes with fiber size variability, rimmed vacuoles, or dystrophic features
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes associated with distal myopathies (e.g., TTN, MATR3, or others)
Electromyography demonstrating myopathic motor unit potentials with early recruitment

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of all three major criteria (clinical distal weakness, early respiratory involvement, and characteristic muscle biopsy findings) with or without supportive genetic or EMG findings
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing is recommended to confirm diagnosis and guide prognosis.

searchTerms: worsening weakness in hands and feet

pathognomonic.symptomName: Early respiratory muscle weakness causing dyspnea
searchTerms: shortness of breath from weak respiratory muscles
difficulty breathing due to muscle weakness
rimmed vacuoles seen in muscle tissue
muscle wasting in hands or feet
loss of muscle bulk in extremities

common.symptomName: Restrictive ventilatory defect on pulmonary function testing
searchTerms: reduced lung volume on breathing tests
mild muscle weakness near body center

common.symptomName: Dysphagia due to oropharyngeal muscle involvement

laboratory: Elevated serum creatine kinase (mild to moderate elevation)
imaging: Muscle MRI showing selective distal muscle atrophy and fatty replacement
Chest imaging may show elevated diaphragm or atelectasis secondary to respiratory muscle weakness
genetic: Pathogenic variants in TTN, MATR3, or other distal myopathy-associated genes
other: Pulmonary function tests showing restrictive pattern

distinguishingFeatures: Predominantly distal leg weakness without early respiratory involvement
Multisystem involvement including cataracts and cardiac conduction defects
Presence of rimmed vacuoles but with more prominent proximal weakness
Associated with mutations in VCP or GNE genes

redFlags: Onset of respiratory symptoms preceding limb weakness
Signs of cardiac involvement such as arrhythmias or heart failure
references: Udd B, et al. Distal myopathies. Handb Clin Neurol. 2019;161:287-305.
Orphanet: Distal myopathy with early respiratory muscle involvement. ORPHA:34521.
Hackman P, et al. Distal myopathy with early respiratory muscle involvement: clinical and genetic features. Neurology. 2017;89(10):1037-1045.
